book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 24 · Head and Face Injuries
title: Traumatic Brain Injury and the BC TBI Protocol

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already restrict spinal motion, manage the airway, give oxygen and score the GCS. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Understand secondary brain injury and pressure inside the skull
  2. Recognize rising ICP, herniation and the main bleeds
  3. Apply the BC TBI protocol: what the PCP adds, and why no TXA

Textbook: Chapter 24, PDF pages 2000–2007 and 2058–2091
slides.say: Welcome back. Today is the second half of Chapter twenty-four: the head and the brain. As EMRs, you already restrict spinal motion, manage the airway, give oxygen, and score the Glasgow Coma Scale. As a PCP, you need to understand what's happening inside the skull, so your numbers mean something. Three goals today. First, understand secondary brain injury and the pressure inside the skull. Second, recognize rising pressure, herniation, and the main bleeds. Third, apply the BC traumatic brain injury protocol: what the PCP adds, and why TXA is not given for an isolated head injury.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天是第二十四章的后半部分：头和脑。作为 EMR，你们已经会限制脊柱活动、管理气道、给氧、做格拉斯哥昏迷评分。作为 PCP，你需要理解颅内发生了什么，你测的数字才有意义。今天三个目标：第一，理解继发性脑损伤和颅内压；第二，识别颅内压升高、脑疝和几种主要的颅内出血；第三，运用 BC 创伤性脑损伤流程：PCP 多做什么，以及为什么单纯颅脑外伤不给 TXA。

slides.title: Scalp and skull: clues on the outside
slides.body:
• Scalp bleeds a lot; rarely causes shock alone in adults (more in kids)
  • Four fractures: linear (about 80%), depressed, basilar, open
  • Linear fracture at the temple → torn artery → epidural bleed
  • Basilar: CSF from ear or nose, raccoon eyes, Battle sign
  • Bruising can take up to 24 h: not seen ≠ not there
slides.say: The scalp has a rich blood supply, so even small cuts bleed a lot. There are four kinds of skull fracture: linear, which is about eighty percent, depressed, basilar, and open. A linear fracture over the temple can tear the middle meningeal artery and cause an epidural bleed. A basilar fracture, at the base of the skull, shows as fluid from the ear or nose, bruising around the eyes, called raccoon eyes, or bruising behind the ear, called Battle sign. But this bruising can take up to twenty-four hours to appear, so its absence on scene rules nothing out.
slides.sayZh: 头皮血供丰富，小伤口也出很多血。颅骨骨折分四种：线性骨折约占百分之八十，还有凹陷性、颅底和开放性骨折。太阳穴附近的线性骨折可能撕裂脑膜中动脉，引起硬膜外出血。颅底骨折表现为耳朵或鼻子流液、眼眶周围瘀斑，叫熊猫眼，或耳后瘀斑，叫 Battle 征。但这些瘀斑可能要二十四小时才出现，所以现场没看到并不能排除。

slides.title: Primary vs secondary brain injury
slides.body:
You can't undo the first hit. You can prevent the second.

Primary injurySecondary injury
At the moment of impactMinutes to days later
Bruising, tearing, bleedingHypoxia, hypotension, hypoglycemia
Can't be reversed on sceneSwelling, rising ICP, infection

The brain is 2% of body weight but uses 20% of the oxygen and 25% of the glucose, with no stores.
slides.say: A brain injury happens in two steps. The primary injury happens at the moment of impact: the brain hits the skull and bruises, tears, or bleeds. Nothing you do on scene can undo that. The secondary injury comes after, from minutes to days later, from low oxygen, low blood pressure, low blood sugar, swelling, and rising pressure in the skull. The brain is only about two percent of body weight, but it uses about twenty percent of the body's oxygen and twenty-five percent of its glucose, with no stores. Your job as a PCP is to prevent them.
slides.sayZh: 脑损伤分两步。原发性损伤发生在撞击的那一刻：脑撞到颅骨，挫伤、撕裂或出血，现场做什么都无法逆转。继发性损伤随后发生，几分钟到几天后都可能，原因是缺氧、低血压、低血糖、脑肿胀和颅内压升高。脑只占体重约百分之二，却消耗全身约百分之二十的氧和百分之二十五的葡萄糖，而且没有储备。作为 PCP，你的工作就是防止它们。

slides.title: Pressure in a closed box: ICP and CPP
slides.body:
CPP = MAP − ICP

  • The adult skull can't expand; normal ICP is 5–15 mm Hg
  • The brain needs a CPP of at least 60 mm Hg
  • One drop below 60 doubles the chance of death
  • Body raises BP → more blood in → higher ICP: a vicious cycle
  • No ICP number on scene: keep BP up, avoid what raises ICP
slides.say: The adult skull is a closed box. Normal pressure inside, the ICP or intracranial pressure, is five to fifteen millimetres of mercury. What the brain needs is perfusion pressure, CPP, which is the mean arterial pressure, the average pressure in the arteries, minus the ICP. In an adult, CPP must stay at sixty or above; a single drop below sixty doubles the chance of death. Raising the blood pressure to compensate pushes in more blood and raises the ICP further: a vicious cycle. You can't measure ICP in the ambulance, so keep the blood pressure up and avoid anything that raises pressure in the skull.
slides.sayZh: 成人颅骨是个封闭的盒子。颅内压，也就是 ICP，正常为五到十五毫米汞柱。脑需要的是灌注压 CPP，它等于平均动脉压，也就是动脉里的平均压力，减去颅内压。成人 CPP 必须保持在六十以上；只要跌破六十一次，死亡几率就翻倍。身体靠升高血压来代偿，却会挤进更多血、让颅内压更高，形成恶性循环。救护车上测不了颅内压，所以要把血压维持住，避免一切会升高颅内压的事。

slides.title: Rising ICP: early and late signs
slides.body:
Earlyheadache, vomiting (often no nausea), altered LOC, seizurespupil slow to react
LateCushing triad, posturingdecorticate (flexion), decerebrate (extension)
Brainstem failingone blown pupil; irregular or no breathingBP falls; few survive

Cushing triad: high BP with widening pulse pressure + slow pulse + irregular breathing. It is not shock.
slides.say: Early signs of rising pressure are headache, vomiting, often without nausea, a changing level of consciousness, and seizures. Later comes the Cushing triad: high blood pressure with a widening pulse pressure, a slow pulse, and irregular breathing. Don't mistake it for shock. Shock gives a fast, weak pulse and cool, clammy skin; Cushing gives a slow, bounding pulse and high pressure. You may also see posturing: decorticate, with the arms flexed toward the core, or decerebrate, with arms and legs stiffly extended. When the lower brainstem fails, one pupil blows, breathing becomes erratic or stops, and the pressure finally falls.
slides.sayZh: 颅内压升高的早期征象是头痛、呕吐（常常没有恶心）、意识水平改变和抽搐。之后出现库欣三联征：血压升高伴脉压增宽、脉搏变慢、呼吸不规则。别把它当成休克：休克是脉搏快而弱、皮肤湿冷；库欣是脉搏慢而有力、血压高。你还可能看到异常姿势：去皮质姿势，双臂向身体中心屈曲；去大脑姿势，四肢僵直伸展。下段脑干衰竭时，一侧瞳孔散大，呼吸紊乱甚至停止，血压最终下降。

slides.q: A 45-year-old fell from a ladder and struck his head. GCS 7. BP 186/102, pulse 52 and bounding, breathing 8/min and irregular, skin warm and dry. What do these findings most likely show?
options: Cushing triad from rising intracranial pressure
Neurogenic shock from a spinal cord injury
A normal stress response to pain
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A forty-five-year-old fell from a ladder and struck his head. His GCS is seven. His blood pressure is one hundred eighty-six over one hundred two, his pulse is fifty-two and bounding, he's breathing eight times a minute, irregularly, and his skin is warm and dry. What do these findings most likely show? A, compensated hypovolemic shock. B, the Cushing triad from rising intracranial pressure. C, neurogenic shock from a spinal cord injury. D, a normal stress response to pain. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一名四十五岁男子从梯子上摔下撞到头，GCS 七分，血压一百八十六比一百零二，脉搏五十二、有力，呼吸每分钟八次且不规则，皮肤温暖干燥。这些表现最可能说明什么？A 代偿期低血容量性休克；B 颅内压升高引起的库欣三联征；C 脊髓损伤导致的神经源性休克；D 对疼痛的正常应激反应。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. High blood pressure with a widening pulse pressure, a slow bounding pulse, and irregular breathing after a head injury make up the Cushing triad, a late sign of rising intracranial pressure. A is wrong: shock gives a fast, weak pulse, fast breathing, and cool, clammy skin. C is wrong because neurogenic shock causes low blood pressure, not high. D doesn't explain a slow pulse, irregular breathing, and a GCS of seven.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。头部受伤后出现血压升高伴脉压增宽、脉搏慢而有力、呼吸不规则，就是库欣三联征，属于颅内压升高的晚期征象。A 错：休克是脉搏快而弱、呼吸快、皮肤湿冷。C 错，因为神经源性休克是低血压而不是高血压。D 解释不了脉搏慢、呼吸不规则和 GCS 七分。

slides.title: The bleeds: epidural vs subdural
slides.body:
EpiduralSubdural
SourceArtery (middle meningeal)Veins (bridging veins)
SpeedFastSlower; chronic up to 2 weeks
Classic pictureOut → lucid interval → out againFluctuating LOC, one-sided weakness
How common0.5–1% of head injuriesAbout 5%
Watch forSame-side pupil blowsOlder adults, alcohol, blood thinners
slides.say: Two bleeds are worth knowing well. An epidural hematoma is blood between the skull and the dura. It usually comes from a temple fracture that tears the middle meningeal artery, so it's fast. The classic story is a brief knockout, then a lucid interval when the patient seems fine, then a rapid slide back into unresponsiveness, with the pupil on the same side blowing. A subdural hematoma lies under the dura, from torn veins, so it develops more slowly, with a fluctuating level of consciousness or weakness on one side. On scene, you don't need to name the bleed; you need to see the pressure rising.
slides.sayZh: 有两种出血要熟悉。硬膜外血肿是颅骨和硬脑膜之间积血，通常是颞部骨折撕裂脑膜中动脉引起的，所以进展很快。典型经过是：短暂昏迷，然后一段中间清醒期，病人看起来没事，随后迅速再次陷入无反应，同侧瞳孔散大。硬膜下血肿在硬脑膜下面，来自撕裂的静脉，所以发展较慢，表现为意识时好时坏或一侧肢体无力。现场你不需要说出是哪种出血，你要看出颅内压正在升高。

slides.title: Concussion, DAI and contusion
slides.body:
Concussionbrain shaken; temporary dysfunctionmay forget events before or after
DAInerve fibres stretched or torndiffuse; often poor outcome
Contusionbruised brain, often the frontal lobeswells → raises ICP

Red flags: repeats the same question, combative, amnesia, one-sided weakness, falling GCS.
slides.say: A concussion happens when the brain is shaken inside the skull. It causes temporary confusion, with or without a loss of consciousness, and the patient may not remember events just before or after the injury. Diffuse axonal injury, or DAI, is more serious: high-speed forces stretch, shear, or tear nerve fibres across the brain, and the outcome is often poor. A contusion is a bruise on the brain, most often in the frontal lobe, and like any bruise it swells, raising the pressure. Listen for red flags: a patient who keeps asking the same question, who is combative, or whose GCS is falling.
slides.sayZh: 脑震荡是脑在颅内被晃动，引起暂时性意识混乱，可有可无意识丧失，病人可能记不起受伤前后的事。弥漫性轴索损伤，简称 DAI，更严重：高速的力把整个脑的神经纤维拉伸、剪切或撕裂，预后常常很差。脑挫伤是脑组织的瘀伤，最常见于额叶，和所有瘀伤一样会肿胀，从而升高颅内压。留意危险信号：病人反复问同一个问题、有攻击性，或 GCS 在下降。

slides.title: Serial neuro checks: the PCP's main tool
slides.body:
• A changing LOC is the single most important sign
  • Baseline AVPU with the time, then GCS at least every 5 min
  • Document every score with its time
  • BC: GCS ≥ 13 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤ 8 severe
  • Pupils: size, equality, reaction, every time

Herniation (book): unresponsive + 2 or more of: unequal or blown pupils; extensor posturing or no motor response; GCS ≤ 8 or a fall of 2+.
slides.say: A change in level of consciousness is the single most important sign, and the direction it's moving matters most. Get a baseline with AVPU and note the time, then score the GCS at least every five minutes, and document each score with its time. BC classifies a GCS of thirteen or more as mild, nine to twelve as moderate, and eight or less as severe. And know the book's signs of herniation: an unresponsive patient with at least two of these: unequal or blown pupils, extensor posturing or no motor response, or a GCS of eight or less or a drop of two points.
slides.sayZh: 意识水平的变化是最重要的单一指标，最关键的是它往哪个方向变。先用 AVPU 定基线并记下时间，然后至少每五分钟评一次 GCS，每个分数都连同时间记录。BC 把 GCS 十三分及以上定为轻度，九到十二分为中度，八分及以下为重度。还要知道书上的脑疝征象：病人无反应，并且至少有以下两项：瞳孔不等大或散大固定；伸展姿势或对疼痛无运动反应；GCS 八分及以下或下降两分以上。

slides.title: Airway and breathing for the injured brain
slides.body:
• Manual stabilization, jaw thrust; expect vomiting → log-roll, suction
  • No nasal airway with a CSF leak or skull base fracture
  • BC: O₂ and ventilations to keep SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Book: ventilate an adult at about 10/min
  • Don't routinely hyperventilate: vessels narrow, less O₂ to the brain
  • Book: 20/min briefly only if herniating; ETCO₂ 35–40, never < 30
slides.say: Low oxygen and high carbon dioxide both make the brain swell, so airway and breathing come first. Hold the head in line and use a jaw thrust. Expect vomiting: be ready to log-roll and suction, because aspiration sharply raises the death rate. No nasal airway if there's fluid from the nose or a suspected skull base fracture. BC asks every licence level to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, assisting ventilations if needed. Don't hyperventilate routinely: it narrows the brain's vessels and starves it of oxygen. The book allows brief faster breathing, twenty a minute, only with signs of herniation.
slides.sayZh: 缺氧和二氧化碳潴留都会让脑肿胀，所以气道和呼吸放在第一位。手法保持头部中立，用推颌法。要预料到呕吐：随时准备整体翻身并吸引，因为误吸会让死亡率大增。鼻子流液或怀疑颅底骨折时不要用鼻咽通气道。BC 要求所有执照级别把血氧维持在九十四以上，必要时辅助通气。不要常规过度通气：它会让脑血管收缩，脑反而缺氧。书上只在有脑疝征象时允许短时加快到每分钟二十次。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC TBI protocol
slides.body:
Suspect TBI in any patient with head trauma and an altered level of consciousness.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Oxygen: SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if needed, keeping SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Head of the bed up 30°
  • Loosen the hard collar

PCP adds

  • Keep blood glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
  • Keep systolic BP > 120 mmHg
  • IV: run TKVO if systolic > 120
  • TXA is contraindicated in isolated TBI
slides.say: Here is the BC traumatic brain injury protocol. BC says to suspect a brain injury in any patient with head trauma and an altered level of consciousness. On the left is what every licence level does: oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, assisted ventilations if breathing is inadequate, the head of the bed raised to thirty degrees, and the hard collar loosened. On the right is what the PCP adds. Keep the blood sugar between four and eight millimoles per litre. Keep the systolic pressure above one hundred twenty; if it's already above one hundred twenty, the IV just runs TKVO, which means to keep the vein open. And TXA is contraindicated for an isolated brain injury.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的创伤性脑损伤流程。BC 规定：任何有头部外伤并伴意识水平改变的病人，都要怀疑脑损伤。左栏是所有执照级别都做的：给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上；呼吸不足时辅助通气；床头抬高三十度；松开硬质颈托。右栏是 PCP 多做的：把血糖维持在每升四到八毫摩尔；把收缩压维持在一百二十以上，如果已经高于一百二十，静脉只以 TKVO 速度滴注，也就是保持静脉通畅；还有，单纯脑损伤禁用 TXA。

slides.title: Glucose and blood pressure: PCP targets
slides.body:
• Check the BGL early and again en route
  • BGL < 4.0: D10W 10–25 g IV (100–250 mL)
  • No IV access? Glucagon
  • Don't overshoot: no dextrose fluids unless the sugar is low
  • Systolic < 120: look for bleeding elsewhere
  • Isolated closed head injury ≠ hypovolemic shock in an adult
slides.say: Glucose first. Check it early and again en route. If it's below four, treat it: D10W, ten to twenty-five grams IV, which is one hundred to two hundred fifty millilitres, or glucagon if you can't get an IV. But don't overshoot: the book warns that dextrose-containing fluids can worsen brain swelling, so give sugar only for a low reading, and aim for four to eight. Now blood pressure. If the systolic falls below one hundred twenty, think beyond the head. In an adult, an isolated closed head injury doesn't cause hypovolemic shock. Look for bleeding in the chest, abdomen, pelvis, or long bones.
slides.sayZh: 先说血糖：早测，途中再测。低于四就要处理：D10W 十到二十五克静脉给，也就是一百到二百五十毫升；开不了静脉就用胰高血糖素。但别矫枉过正：书上提醒含糖液体会加重脑水肿，所以只在血糖低时补糖，目标是四到八。再说血压。收缩压低于一百二十时，要想到头以外的地方。成人单纯闭合性颅脑伤不会导致低血容量性休克。要找胸腔、腹腔、骨盆或长骨的出血。

slides.q: You are a PCP. A 30-year-old cyclist hit his head 40 minutes ago. Isolated head injury, GCS 11, BP 138/84, BGL 6.1 mmol/L, SpO₂ 95% on oxygen. Which plan fits the BC TBI protocol?
options: Give TXA 2 g IV push over 1 minute
Head of the bed up 30°, loosen the collar, IV at TKVO, GCS and pupils every 5 minutes
Give a 20 mL/kg bolus to protect the brain
Ventilate at 20 breaths per minute to lower the ICP
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A thirty-year-old cyclist hit his head forty minutes ago. It's an isolated head injury. His GCS is eleven, blood pressure one hundred thirty-eight over eighty-four, blood sugar six point one, and saturation ninety-five percent on oxygen. Which plan fits the BC TBI protocol? A, give TXA two grams IV push over one minute. B, head of the bed up thirty degrees, loosen the collar, IV at TKVO, and GCS and pupils every five minutes. C, give a twenty millilitre per kilogram bolus to protect the brain. D, ventilate at twenty breaths a minute to lower the pressure in the skull. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名三十岁的骑车人四十分钟前撞到头，是单纯颅脑外伤。GCS 十一分，血压一百三十八比八十四，血糖六点一，吸氧下血氧九十五。哪个方案符合 BC 的 TBI 流程？A 给 TXA 两克静脉推注、一分钟推完；B 床头抬高三十度、松开颈托、静脉 TKVO、每五分钟查 GCS 和瞳孔；C 按每公斤二十毫升推注补液来保护大脑；D 每分钟通气二十次来降低颅内压。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Raising the head thirty degrees and loosening the collar apply at every licence level, and because his systolic is above one hundred twenty, the PCP runs the IV at TKVO and keeps reassessing. A is wrong: TXA is contraindicated in an isolated TBI. C is wrong because his pressure already meets the BC target, so a bolus isn't needed. D is wrong: routine hyperventilation narrows the brain's vessels, and he shows no signs of herniation.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。床头抬高三十度、松开颈托是所有执照级别都做的；他的收缩压高于一百二十，所以 PCP 让静脉以 TKVO 速度滴注并持续复评。A 错：单纯 TBI 禁用 TXA。C 错，因为他的血压已经达到 BC 目标，不需要推注补液。D 错：常规过度通气会让脑血管收缩，而且他没有脑疝征象。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Systolic target: book ≥ 90 → BC > 120 mmHg
  • Head position: book's TBI section silent → BC bed up 30°, collar loose
  • Glucose: book treats < 4 only → BC keeps 4.0–8.0; D10W only
  • GCS: book 13–14 mild → BC ≥ 13 mild
  • Mannitol, hypertonic saline, lidocaine: not on the BC exam drug list
  • Benzodiazepines: not on the licensing exam
slides.say: On the BC exam, BC wins. The book's ninety-ninety-nine rule says a single saturation under ninety percent, a systolic under ninety, or a GCS falling two points to eight or less raises the risk of death, so it aims for a systolic of at least ninety. BC sets a higher target: above one hundred twenty. The book's brain injury section doesn't raise the head; BC raises the bed thirty degrees and loosens the collar. The book gives glucose only below four; BC keeps it between four and eight, with D10W as its only IV dextrose. The book's mannitol, hypertonic saline, and lidocaine aren't on the BC exam drug list, and benzodiazepines aren't on the licensing exam either.
slides.sayZh: 在 BC 考试里以 BC 为准。书上的 90-90-9 规则说：血氧一次低于百分之九十、收缩压一次低于九十，或 GCS 下降两分到八分及以下，都会升高死亡风险，所以书上的收缩压目标是至少九十。BC 的目标更高：一百二十以上。书上脑损伤的部分没有抬高头部；BC 要求床头抬高三十度并松开颈托。书上只在血糖低于四时才给糖；BC 要求维持在四到八之间，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。书上的甘露醇、高渗盐水和利多卡因不在 BC 考纲药物范围内，苯二氮卓类执照考试也不考。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• TXA: contraindicated in an isolated head injury
  • Head injury + bleeding shock elsewhere: other TXA rules still apply
  • Systolic > 120 → IV at TKVO; no fluid "just in case"
  • Correct a low sugar; don't push it high
  • Methoxyflurane: not with head injury; Entonox: not with altered LOC
  • Destination: trauma centre with neurosurgery (book)
slides.say: Now the watch-outs that are new at PCP level. First, TXA is contraindicated in an isolated head injury. Read the word isolated carefully, though: if the patient also has shock from bleeding elsewhere, the head injury alone doesn't stop you, but every other TXA rule still applies, like the three-hour limit and no patients under twelve. Second, if the systolic is above one hundred twenty, the IV runs TKVO; no fluid just in case. Third, correct a low sugar, but don't push it high. Fourth, pain relief: methoxyflurane is contraindicated with a head injury, and Entonox with an altered level of consciousness.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 层面新的注意事项。第一，单纯颅脑外伤禁用 TXA。但要读准「单纯」这个词：如果病人同时有其他部位出血导致的休克，单是颅脑外伤并不阻止你，但 TXA 的其他规定照样适用，比如受伤超过三小时不给、未满十二岁不给。第二，收缩压高于一百二十时静脉只走 TKVO，不要「以防万一」地补液。第三，低血糖要纠正，但不要把血糖推得太高。第四，镇痛：头部外伤禁用甲氧氟烷，意识改变禁用笑气。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Prevent the second hit: hypoxia, hypotension, low sugar
  2. Trend GCS and pupils every 5 min; the Cushing triad is not shock
  3. BC: SpO₂ ≥ 94%, bed 30°, collar loose; PCP: BGL 4–8, systolic > 120

IV at TKVO if systolic > 120. No TXA for an isolated TBI.

Next: Chapter 25 — spine injuries
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: you can't undo the first hit, but you can prevent the second: low oxygen, low blood pressure, and low blood sugar. Two: trend the GCS and pupils at least every five minutes, and remember that the Cushing triad means rising pressure in the skull, not shock. Three: the BC TBI protocol. Everyone keeps the saturation at ninety-four or higher, raises the head thirty degrees, and loosens the collar. The PCP adds a blood sugar of four to eight, a systolic above one hundred twenty with the IV at TKVO, and no TXA for an isolated brain injury. Next time: Chapter twenty-five, spine injuries. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 三句话收尾。一，第一次打击无法挽回，但你能防止第二次：缺氧、低血压和低血糖。二，至少每五分钟追踪 GCS 和瞳孔；记住库欣三联征说明颅内压升高，不是休克。三，BC 的 TBI 流程：所有人都要保持血氧九十四以上、床头抬高三十度、松开颈托；PCP 多做的是血糖维持四到八、收缩压一百二十以上并让静脉走 TKVO，单纯脑损伤不给 TXA。下节课讲第二十五章，脊柱损伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
